statement: For conditions other than PTSD, evidence is insufficient to say whether MDMA-assisted therapy helps. The systematic reviews read here (searches up to March 2024) found only small studies outside PTSD: one randomized trial each in anxiety related to a life-threatening illness (18 people), social anxiety in autistic adults (12) and tinnitus (13), an open-label study in alcohol use disorder (14), an uncontrolled study of couples in which one partner has PTSD (6 couples) and a Swiss case series. The Cochrane review rated the evidence in life-threatening illness very uncertain: in its one trial, MDMA against placebo changed trait anxiety by −14.7 points on a 20 to 80 scale (95% CI −29.45 to 0.05) and depression by −6.3 points on a 0 to 63 scale (−16.93 to 4.33). A network meta-analysis of depressive symptoms, whose MDMA trials were mostly in PTSD, found high-dose MDMA better than the placebo arms of psychedelic trials by 5.3 HAMD-17 points (95% credible interval 2.26 to 8.32) but not clearly better than the placebo arms of antidepressant trials (1.5, −2.79 to 5.78), a comparison made only indirectly. A critical narrative review found that, for MDMA, only the two phase 3 PTSD trials met its minimum standard (randomized, more than 15 people per group) and called MDMA for PTSD a signal needing replication. The reviews report that blinding was rarely achieved and that controlled follow-up was short. Certainty: very low. Status: single study (one trial per condition outside PTSD).
plain: The reviews up to 2024 found only a few very small studies of MDMA therapy outside PTSD: in people anxious about a life-threatening illness, autistic adults with social anxiety, people with tinnitus, people with alcohol problems and couples. Each had one small trial or no comparison group at all. The best review says the results for serious illness are very uncertain. So nobody can yet say whether MDMA therapy helps any of these conditions.
population: People with conditions other than PTSD: anxiety related to a life-threatening illness, social anxiety in autistic adults, tinnitus, alcohol use disorder, couples with one partner with PTSD, depressive symptoms
exposure: MDMA-assisted therapy (MDMA in one to three sessions with psychotherapy)
comparator: Placebo or low-dose MDMA with the same therapy; none in open-label and uncontrolled studies
outcome: Condition-specific symptoms (anxiety, depression); number and design of the trials available
magnitude: Life-threatening illness (Cochrane, 1 trial, 18): STAI-T −14.70 (95% CI −29.45 to 0.05), STAI-S −16.10 (−33.03 to 0.83), BDI-II −6.30 (−16.93 to 4.33), very low certainty. Depressive symptoms (network meta-analysis; MDMA trials mostly PTSD): high-dose MDMA against psychedelic-trial placebo 5.32 HAMD-17 points (2.26 to 8.32); against antidepressant-trial placebo 1.53 (−2.79 to 5.78). Studies outside PTSD: randomized, 18, 12 and 13 participants; open-label, 14 (alcohol use disorder); uncontrolled, 6 couples.

evidence.locator: Results › Effects of interventions › Entactogens (MDMA) › Anxiety and Depression; Summary of findings 2
evidence.extracted: One trial (Wolfson 2020; 18 participants): STAI-T mean difference −14.70 (95% CI −29.45 to 0.05) and STAI-S −16.10 (−33.03 to 0.83), both on 20 to 80 scales; BDI-II −6.30 (−16.93 to 4.33) on a 0 to 63 scale; 1 month after the second session; very low certainty, downgraded once for risk of bias and twice for imprecision.

evidence.locator: Results › Description of studies › Included studies, 1st paragraph; Ongoing studies
evidence.extracted: Searched on 30 March 2024: of six randomized trials in people with life-threatening diseases, one evaluated MDMA (18 randomized and analysed); seven ongoing trials, of psilocybin, LSD and ketamine, none of MDMA.

evidence.locator: Results › MDMA, 1st paragraph; Table 1 (Other disorders rows)
evidence.extracted: Besides PTSD, randomized trials of MDMA in end-of-life anxiety (Wolfson 2020, 13 MDMA and 5 placebo), social anxiety in adults with autism (Danforth 2018, 12) and tinnitus (Searchfield 2020, 13), and an open-label study in alcohol use disorder (Sessa 2019, 2021; 14).

Of 13 studies to October 2023, the only randomized trial outside PTSD was in autistic adults with social anxiety (12); others outside PTSD were an open-label alcohol use disorder study (14) and a Swiss case series of various treatment-resistant disorders; the uncontrolled couples study (6 couples) enrolled dyads with one partner with PTSD.

evidence.locator: Fig. 2, upper and middle panels (values printed in the figure image); Results › Network meta-analysis, 1st paragraph; Discussion › Strengths and limitations of this study, 2nd paragraph
evidence.extracted: High-dose MDMA against the placebo arms of psychedelic trials 5.32 HAMD-17 points (95% CrI 2.26 to 8.32); against the placebo arms of escitalopram trials 1.53 (−2.79 to 5.78), the two parts of the network being joined only by one head-to-head psilocybin-escitalopram trial; participants in the MDMA trials were predominantly diagnosed with PTSD, those in the escitalopram trials with major depressive disorder.

evidence.locator: Minimal research quality standards imposed in this review, 3rd paragraph; Safety and Effectiveness of Psychedelic Drugs › MDMA for post-traumatic stress disorder, 1st paragraph; Summary of Effectiveness Evidence for Psychedelic Medicines, 4th paragraph
evidence.extracted: Standard: randomized trials in diagnosed disorders with more than 15 participants per condition; for MDMA only the two phase 3 PTSD trials, run by a consortium funded by MAPS, are discussed; because of absent successful blinding and likely expectancy effects, MDMA for PTSD is a positive signal that should not be taken as definitive without replication in methodologically stronger studies.

evidence.locator: Results › Risk of bias in included studies, 1st paragraph; Results › Effects of interventions, 2nd paragraph; Characteristics of included studies › Wolfson 2020 (risk-of-bias table)
evidence.extracted: Blinding could not be achieved in any included trial; in the MDMA trial more than 80% of investigators and participants guessed the assignment correctly and most outcomes were self-reported; all outcomes after more than 3 months were measured after crossover, without a comparison group.

risk_of_bias.note: Blinding not achieved in the trials; self-reported outcomes.

indirectness.note: Not rated down separately: the claim reports the depression estimates as coming from trials mostly in PTSD.

imprecision.note: One small trial per condition; intervals include no effect.

grade.reasoning: The underlying evidence for each condition outside PTSD is one small randomized trial or an uncontrolled study, as found by systematic reviews searched up to October 2023 and March 2024. Starting from randomized trials, rated down once for risk of bias (unblinding) and twice for imprecision, giving very low certainty, which matches the Cochrane rating for MDMA. The claim states insufficient evidence rather than no effect: the point estimates in the life-threatening-illness trial favour MDMA, but the intervals include no effect. Trials published after these searches (read by another reader) are for the editor to join.
